build.prompt_version: Trump Diary Phase 1 Discovery Prompt v1

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Immigration enforcement as carceral, militarized, and ideological social control
candidate_threads.description: Across the window, immigration policy is repeatedly used not just for border management but as a broader method of coercive governance: militarized raids, detention expansion, data-sharing, ideological vetting, third-country deportation, service exclusion, and intimidation of sanctuary jurisdictions. The recurring pattern is a rights-light enforcement architecture that can discipline migrants, mixed-status communities, protesters, students, and local governments.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration becomes an authoritarian laboratory: militarized raids, TPS terminations, and third-country deportations
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Explicitly frames immigration as a proving ground for extreme state power, combining deportation policy, militarized raids, detention abuse, and oversight rollback.

supporting_developments.development_title: Militarized policing and protest suppression align security forces with regime preservation
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds the security-force dimension to immigration enforcement, including Guard/Marines and violent raids tied to immigration protests and detention.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration enforcement hardens into a militarized, data-driven regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly captures the recurring pattern of raids, expanded detention powers, surveillance, and data-sharing as a systemic enforcement model.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration enforcement becomes a militarized, data‑driven control system
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows continuity through budget surges, mega-detention, National Guard support, Medicaid data access, and courthouse arrests.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration, gender, and benefits: stratifying citizenship and rights
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the thread from enforcement mechanics into differentiated rights and benefits based on status and identity.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and Detention Regime Becomes a Domestic Carceral Archipelago
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Emphasizes detention black holes, camp infrastructure, arbitrary arrests, and expansion of coercive confinement beyond classic immigration processing.

supporting_developments.development_title: Citizenship and Social Rights Are Reshaped Along Ancestry, Ideology, and Status Lines
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows immigration control linked to ancestry-based belonging, parole termination, and welfare exclusion.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration, detention, and homelessness policy harden into a carceral governance model
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Continues the pattern through expanded military involvement, detention growth, ICE funding surges, and carceral treatment of migrants and the poor.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration enforcement becomes a tool of fear, punishment, and profit
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Highlights intimidation of immigrant communities and sanctuary jurisdictions alongside privatized detention expansion.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and visas become an ideological sorting system backed by militarized enforcement
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Makes explicit the ideological-vetting layer: student visa revocations, continuous vetting, TPS termination, third-country deportation, and militarized branding.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration enforcement and social policy deepen a tiered citizenship regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Links detention abuses and opaque ICE transfers to broader second-class citizenship for migrants and other targeted groups.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration enforcement hardens into a sprawling, politicized security apparatus
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows apparatus-building through hiring, local-police incentives, USCIS arrest powers, and asylum restrictions.

supporting_developments.development_title: Surveillance and outsourcing expand state reach over immigrants and critics
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds the surveillance-contractor layer to the same enforcement architecture.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration enforcement becomes a paramilitary campaign against immigrant communities
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Confirms sustained continuity via workplace raids, fatal force, service exclusion, global asylum restrictions, and campaigns against sanctuary protections.

aliases: ideological sorting through visas and deportation
inclusion_notes: Include raids, detention expansion, deportation policy, third-country removals, ideological vetting, surveillance/data-sharing, and punishment of sanctuary jurisdictions when they form one coercive system.
Include rights-stratification effects on noncitizens, asylum seekers, visa holders, and mixed-status families when tied to immigration governance.
Include military or National Guard support when used in service of immigration enforcement.
exclusion_notes: Exclude broader generic protest suppression unless the enforcement action is clearly rooted in immigration operations or anti-immigrant governance.
Exclude standalone voting/citizenship-rule fights unless they directly concern immigration status as an instrument of state control.
boundary_notes: Overlaps with cand_SECURITY_FORCES_FOR_DOMESTIC_CONTROL, but this thread is anchored in immigration governance rather than domestic security doctrine generally.
Overlaps with cand_TIERED_CITIZENSHIP_AND_TARGETED_RIGHTS, but this thread centers the enforcement machinery more than the normative hierarchy of belonging.
Can absorb narrower labels about ICE expansion, detention camps, or visa vetting as subcomponents.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge later with window candidates labeled around 'immigration as authoritarian laboratory,' 'ICE militarization,' or 'detention regime expansion'.
Could later split if the year-level corpus distinguishes 'detention/militarization' from 'ideological visa/citizenship screening'.
split_suggestions: Possible future split between physical carceral enforcement and immigration-linked data/surveillance if both become very large year-wide.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Administrative state capture through purges, loyalist appointments, and dismantling of neutral expertise
candidate_threads.description: A recurring throughline in the window is the conversion of agencies from professional or semi-independent institutions into tools of presidential control. This includes civil-service purges, Schedule G-style politicization, installation of loyalists, stripping of union protections, firing or intimidating data and science officials, and hollowing out watchdog or expert capacity across health, justice, diplomacy, intelligence, and regulatory agencies.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil service and foreign-policy apparatus hollowed out and repopulated with loyalists
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly identifies purges, reorganization, and replacement of expertise with loyalty across national security and diplomacy.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil service and key agencies are purged and politicized
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Captures the structural mechanism of hiring-rule changes, firings, and ideological restructuring across agencies.

supporting_developments.development_title: Administrative State Captured Through AI Deregulation and Loyalist Appointments
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows agency capture via AI-based deregulation, expert-body purges, and appointment of loyalists in legal and prosecutorial roles.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive capture and hollowing-out of neutral institutions and public services
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the pattern to statistical agencies, CFPB, USAID, VA, and other neutral institutions being politicized or privatized.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil service, unions, and independent data guardians are purged or politicized
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds union contract cancellation, intelligence-staff cuts, BLS purges, and attacks on independent officials as part of the same project.

supporting_developments.development_title: Public health and emergency agencies are purged and politicized
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows political control over CDC and FEMA, retaliation against internal dissent, and loss of civil-service protections.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil service, public health, and environmental agencies purged and politicized
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Continues the same pattern through public-health cuts, environmental retaliation, VOA layoffs, and suppression of whistleblowers.

supporting_developments.development_title: Courts and Congress tilt toward executive and ideological priorities over independent checks
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows how judicial and congressional choices are helping normalize control over independent agencies and removals.

inclusion_notes: Include firings, reclassification, staff purges, union-rights removal, loyalist appointments, and intimidation of expert officials across agencies.
Include capture of health, science, intelligence, diplomacy, and regulatory bodies when framed as replacing neutrality with obedience.
Include court or congressional moves that enable easier removal of protected officials when part of the same administrative-control pattern.
exclusion_notes: Exclude generic deregulatory policy if it does not involve institutional capture or staffing/control mechanisms.
Exclude information-control stories unless they primarily concern who controls the bureaucracy rather than public narrative outputs.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_INFO_CONTROL_AND_RECORD_MANIPULATION: this thread is about who controls institutions, not mainly what information they emit.
Distinct from cand_ECONOMIC_CRONYISM_AND_EXECUTIVE_POLITICAL_ECONOMY: privatization belongs here only when used to hollow out neutral state capacity.
Closely related to cand_ATTACK_ON_LABOR_AND_COLLECTIVE_COUNTERPOWER where federal unions are targeted as part of bureaucratic subordination.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with labels such as 'administrative state capture,' 'civil-service purge,' or 'agency loyalization' from other windows.
split_suggestions: Could later separate 'personnel capture' from 'destruction of expert/public-service capacity' if the year-wide catalogue needs finer resolution.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Law used as a weapon against opponents while allies and elite-linked misconduct receive protection or opacity
candidate_threads.description: A major continuity thread in the window is the selective use of prosecutorial, judicial, and investigatory power: critics, investigators, immigrants, and political opponents face raids, subpoenas, grand juries, or rhetorical criminalization, while Trump allies or elite-linked scandals are handled through secrecy, leniency, pardons, or curated disclosure. The pattern is not simply legal conflict, but asymmetric rule of law.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law and courts weaponized against opponents while elite-linked misconduct stays opaque
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: This development names the pattern directly: law against opponents, opacity for Trump-linked or elite misconduct.

supporting_developments.development_title: Epstein files saga exposes elite impunity and weaponized transparency
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows one major expression of the thread through selective disclosures and scandal management around elite abuse.

supporting_developments.development_title: Rule of law bends toward allies and away from civil rights accountability
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds selective prosecutions, lenient treatment for allies, and rollback of civil-rights enforcement.

supporting_developments.development_title: Epstein files and Obama 'treason': executive power, secrecy, and weaponized investigations
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Strong evidence of both sides of the pattern: criminalizing predecessors while controlling damaging files.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law and Prosecution Turned Against Political and Cultural Opponents
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows explicit threats to prosecute political/cultural targets alongside hints of leniency for Maxwell.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law enforcement and courts are weaponized to protect Trump and punish investigators
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly supports the thread through retaliation against prior Trump investigators and secrecy around Epstein.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law as a shield for allies and a weapon against critics and institutions
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Continues the same pattern through pardons, politicized investigations, and selective transparency.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law enforcement and courts are weaponized against critics while elite-linked cases are shielded
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows raids, opponent-targeting, and slow-walked elite accountability in the same week.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information control and elite impunity: Epstein secrecy, intelligence meddling, and economic spin
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Keeps the elite-impunity side of the thread alive through DOJ dismissal efforts, sealing, FOIA delay, and selective release.

aliases: law as protection for allies and punishment for opponents
inclusion_notes: Include prosecutions, subpoenas, raids, grand juries, pardons, clemency, and document-release strategies when they reflect asymmetric treatment of allies versus opponents.
Include elite scandal management, especially Epstein/Maxwell, when it illustrates curated secrecy or impunity.
Include retaliatory investigations of prior investigators, prosecutors, judges, or political enemies.
exclusion_notes: Exclude generic court deference or executive-power rulings unless they clearly feed asymmetric punishment/protection.
Exclude ordinary administrative purges unless legal process itself is being weaponized.
boundary_notes: Related to cand_INFO_CONTROL_AND_RECORD_MANIPULATION, but here the core mechanism is legal asymmetry, not narrative management alone.
Related to cand_ADMINISTRATIVE_STATE_CAPTURE_AND_LOYALIST_PURGE, but this thread concerns outputs of captured legal institutions rather than personnel control itself.
Can overlap with immigration lawfare, but immigration-specific enforcement should remain primarily under cand_IMMIGRATION_AS_CARCERAL_AND_IDEOLOGICAL_CONTROL unless the asymmetry of law is central.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with labels like 'weaponized DOJ,' 'lawfare against opponents,' or 'impunity for allies' from other windows.
split_suggestions: Could later split into 'political retaliation/investigations' and 'elite scandal opacity/pardons' if needed.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Information control, propaganda, and manipulation of public records, data, and memory
candidate_threads.description: Throughout the window, the administration and allies repeatedly reshape the information environment: press intimidation, public-media cuts, manipulated or suppressed statistics, altered archives, Smithsonian or historical curation, AI propaganda, and selective disclosure of politically sensitive records. The common thread is state-backed control over what the public can know, verify, remember, or treat as legitimate truth.

supporting_developments.development_title: Public health, science, and climate information are captured by ideology and misinformation
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Introduces the broader pattern of official misinformation and degradation of credible public knowledge.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information space and economic data are reshaped to favor the regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly addresses cuts to public media, data withholding, and pressure on information institutions.

supporting_developments.development_title: Assault on independent media and information norms at home and abroad
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Strong evidence of attacks on critical media, press-pool control, and altered human-rights reporting.

supporting_developments.development_title: Disinformation, AI tools, and extremist rhetoric reshape political reality
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds AI propaganda, bot amplification, extremist messaging, and curated archives.

supporting_developments.development_title: Media, Data, and Archives Bent to Protect the President and Shape Reality
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows media-market control, firing data officials, archive pressure, and manipulation of damaging records.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump tightens personal control over economic and scientific data
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Contributes the politicization of official data and science to fit presidential narratives.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information, archives, and education are curated to favor the regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Broadens the thread to official records, universities, lawsuits against media, and perception-shaping through data/algorithms.

supporting_developments.development_title: Control over history, information, and identity tightens across federal institutions
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Captures museum/history curation, politicized intelligence disclosures, gendered language shifts, and contested transparency.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump escalates ideological control over information, history, and public memory
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows attacks on experts, reshaped data, targeted history institutions, and curated foreign-policy narratives.

supporting_developments.development_title: Media, memory, and culture are reshaped to favor state-aligned narratives
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the pattern through public-media starvation, architectural symbolism, Confederate imagery, and bureaucratic memory management.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information space reshaped: public media weakened, disinformation and narrative control rise
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly connects public-media weakening to economic and public-health disinformation and historical narrative fights.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information control and elite impunity: Epstein secrecy, intelligence meddling, and economic spin
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows suppression, recall, delay, and spin across DOJ, intelligence, and economic agencies.

supporting_developments.development_title: AI, media, and propaganda tools are folded into an authoritarian messaging ecosystem
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds AI-generated intimidation, embedded influencers, and a propaganda ecosystem tied to state action.

inclusion_notes: Include manipulation or suppression of statistics, archives, museum/history narratives, public broadcasting, press access, AI propaganda, and selective disclosures.
Include official or quasi-official efforts to flood the zone with misleading claims when tied to governance rather than ordinary partisan spin.
Include information-control actions in health, climate, or economic data when they shape public truth conditions.
exclusion_notes: Exclude legal retaliation stories unless narrative or records control is central.
Exclude mere ideological rhetoric unless linked to institutions, platforms, data systems, or official recordkeeping.
boundary_notes: This thread is about the information environment and memory infrastructure; it intersects with cand_LAW_AS_WEAPON_AND_IMPUNITY_FOR_ALLIES when secrecy around scandals is legal as well as informational.
Distinct from cand_ADMINISTRATIVE_STATE_CAPTURE_AND_LOYALIST_PURGE, which is about controlling institutions internally; this thread is about outputs, narratives, records, and public knowledge.
May overlap with cand_RELIGION_AND_NATIONALIST_SYMBOLIC_ORDER when symbolic politics involve historical memory curation.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with year-wide labels such as 'information control,' 'record erasure,' 'propaganda state,' or 'memory politics'.
split_suggestions: Possible later split between 'media/data suppression' and 'historical-memory/symbolic curation' if those strands persist separately.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Elections and representation re-engineered through gerrymanders, voter restrictions, and executive-election interference
candidate_threads.description: Across the window, representation and electoral procedure are repeatedly manipulated through mid-decade redistricting, coercion of legislators, plans to exclude undocumented residents from census-based representation, mail-voting restrictions, proof-of-citizenship and database projects, and rhetoric about emergency control of elections. The thread is broader than 'voting rights' alone: it concerns structural redesign of who counts, who votes, and how power is allocated.

supporting_developments.development_title: Voting rights and representation erode through courts and redistricting fights
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Establishes the pattern via maps, registration rules, and criminalization of legislative resistance.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive power expands over domestic life: homelessness, college sports, and redistricting
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Includes direct White House intervention in Texas redistricting and election-related federal encroachment.

supporting_developments.development_title: Federalism as Battleground: States Resist and Reinforce Authoritarian Drift
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows state-level gerrymanders, initiative rollbacks, and democratic resistance as part of electoral struggle.

supporting_developments.development_title: Representation is engineered through gerrymanders, coercion, and a skewed census
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Strongly supports the thread through mid-decade remaps, coercive tactics, census exclusion plans, and lawmaker tracking.

supporting_developments.development_title: Redistricting and representation turn into an interstate partisan arms race
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows sustained continuity and escalation via Texas/California retaliatory map battles.

supporting_developments.development_title: Elections and representation are re-engineered through gerrymanders and attacks on voting methods
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Combines redistricting with national attacks on mail voting, machines, citizenship standards, and election legitimacy.

supporting_developments.development_title: Elections and representation are reshaped through gerrymanders and attacks on voting methods
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Continues the same architecture through a draft EO ending mail voting and court fights over maps.

supporting_developments.development_title: Elections and opposition targeted through voter restrictions and selective law enforcement
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds nationwide voter ID, mail-voting limits, barriers to naturalization-based registration, and DOJ asymmetry.

supporting_developments.development_title: Elections and representation are quietly re-engineered through law and data
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows national voter database work, emergency-election talk, gerrymandered maps, and closed-door electoral governance.

aliases: skewed census and voter eligibility control
inclusion_notes: Include redistricting, census/population-count manipulation, mail-voting restrictions, registration barriers, national voting databases, and emergency-election control rhetoric.
Include coercion or punishment of lawmakers when used to force map changes or election-structure outcomes.
Include state and federal rule changes that alter effective political representation.
exclusion_notes: Exclude generic protest suppression unless directly tied to electoral procedure or legislative quorum fights.
Exclude immigration enforcement except where citizenship/counting rules affect representation or access to the franchise.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_TIERED_CITIZENSHIP_AND_TARGETED_RIGHTS: that thread concerns belonging and protection broadly; this one concerns institutional electoral allocation and participation.
Related to cand_LAW_AS_WEAPON_AND_IMPUNITY_FOR_ALLIES where DOJ is selectively used against opposition fundraising or election actors.
Could become a super-thread with children for 'redistricting/census engineering' and 'voting-method restrictions' in a later phase, but within this window they cohere well together.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with labels like 'election engineering,' 'representation manipulation,' or 'voting restriction and gerrymandering' from other windows.
split_suggestions: Possible later split into 'map/census engineering' versus 'voting administration and access restrictions'.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Security forces and emergency powers repurposed for domestic political control
candidate_threads.description: A visible continuity thread in the latter half of the window is the use of police, Guard, federal agents, military framing, and emergency declarations to dominate domestic space, especially in opposition-run cities and protest contexts. While overlapping with immigration enforcement, this thread is broader: it includes D.C. federalization, urban troop deployments, reframing dissent as criminal threat, and the erosion of local self-government through security pretexts.

supporting_developments.development_title: Militarized policing and protest suppression align security forces with regime preservation
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Early window evidence that security institutions are being used for intimidation and protest suppression beyond ordinary policing.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive power and security forces are deployed for spectacle and personal leverage
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows security deployments and executive theatrics used for dominance and leverage over local authority.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump moves to seize lasting control over Washington, D.C. policing and governance
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Strong evidence of emergency-based federalization of local policing and threats to Home Rule.

supporting_developments.development_title: Security forces are repurposed for regime priorities at home and abroad
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Captures the broader repurposing of law enforcement and military tools toward partisan or ideological ends.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump consolidates militarized control over Washington, D.C. and rewires local justice
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Escalates the same thread via Guard deployment, armed patrols, JAG insertion, and prosecutorial rewiring in D.C.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump consolidates direct control over policing and security in D.C. and targets Democratic cities
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the pattern to threats against Baltimore and symbolic occupation of the capital and blue jurisdictions.

supporting_developments.development_title: Emergency rhetoric and security forces are used to suppress protest and redefine dissent as crime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows security logic expanding into protest suppression, flag-burning prosecutions, and emergency framing.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump centralizes power through executive orders, military symbolism, and security-state moves
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds military symbolism, clearances, and national-security personalization to the domestic-control pattern.

supporting_developments.development_title: Protest, Epstein accountability, and DC policing collide in a contest over dissent
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Links militarized patrols and protest criminalization in D.C. to broader suppression of dissent.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump militarizes domestic governance in DC, Chicago, and beyond
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Confirms sustained continuity through Guard deployments, occupation logic, and city-targeted militarization.

supporting_developments.development_title: Charlie Kirk’s assassination is weaponized to punish dissent and reshape public memory
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows how domestic-security framing after violence is used to justify crackdowns on critics.

aliases: troops and agents for regime preservation
inclusion_notes: Include emergency declarations, Guard/federal deployments, Home Rule override attempts, and security-force uses aimed at controlling cities, protests, or domestic political space.
Include criminalization of dissent where it relies on security rhetoric and coercive institutions.
Include military/legal crossovers such as JAG involvement in civilian justice when tied to domestic control.
exclusion_notes: Exclude immigration enforcement incidents when their main logic is migrant control rather than broader urban/domestic power projection.
Exclude generic foreign-policy militarism unless clearly feeding domestic governance methods.
boundary_notes: Adjacent to cand_IMMIGRATION_AS_CARCERAL_AND_IDEOLOGICAL_CONTROL, but broader and centered on domestic jurisdictional control and emergency policing.
Adjacent to cand_LAW_AS_WEAPON_AND_IMPUNITY_FOR_ALLIES, but this thread emphasizes coercive force and emergency governance rather than legal asymmetry per se.
May later merge with year-wide 'militarized domestic governance' candidates.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with labels like 'domestic militarization,' 'federalized policing,' or 'emergency governance over cities'.
split_suggestions: Could later split into 'city takeovers/Home Rule attacks' and 'protest criminalization/security rhetoric' if needed.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Executive political economy of tariffs, crony deals, and inequality-shifting policy
candidate_threads.description: Another recurring thread is the use of economic power as a personalized governing instrument: emergency tariffs, politically targeted trade moves, privatization, donor- or ally-friendly regulatory changes, federal stakes in favored firms, social spending cuts, and protection for insider business interests. The continuity lies less in 'the economy' as a topic than in executive-centered, loyalty-sensitive economic governance that shifts risk downward and advantages insiders.

supporting_developments.development_title: Economic and fiscal policy lock in inequality and crony capitalism under a chaotic tariff regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Strong early statement of the thread via tariffs, tax/spending choices, contractor gains, and inequality hardwiring.

supporting_developments.development_title: Public goods hollowed out while crony capitalism and foreign entanglements deepen
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows defunding of public goods alongside Trump-linked business ventures and donor-friendly policy shifts.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crypto, AI, and crony capitalism: national policy re‑engineered around insider tech interests
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds insider-oriented crypto and AI policy as a newer expression of personalized political economy.

supporting_developments.development_title: Fiscal and trade policy lock in inequality and executive leverage over public goods
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Highlights tariffs, spending leverage, and cuts to public goods as instruments of executive advantage.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive Power and Trade Policy Are Recast as a Personal Economic Weapon
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Strongly supports the thread through tariffs, rescissions, social spending cuts, and prestige/crony projects.

supporting_developments.development_title: Economic policy fuses protectionism, inequality, and crony capitalism
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Captures tariffs as political weapons, upward redistribution, and consolidation/capture.

supporting_developments.development_title: Foreign money and private donors blur the line between public office and personal enrichment
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds foreign gifts and privately funded presidential projects as enrichment-linked political economy.

supporting_developments.development_title: State-capitalist deals and deregulation deepen crony control over the economy and environment
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows direct bargaining with firms, extractive deals, and executive-centered economic management.

supporting_developments.development_title: Inequality is deepened through education, health, and disaster policy choices
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds the inequality-shifting side of the thread through policy designs that burden vulnerable populations.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony industrial policy and tariff shocks concentrate economic power in the presidency
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Provides direct continuity through federal stakes in firms, de minimis termination, and executive control over industry and trade.

supporting_developments.development_title: Labor, workers, and universities squeezed as economic policy favors elites
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows ongoing tariff misrepresentation, anti-labor policy, and funding leverage that benefits elites while disciplining institutions.

inclusion_notes: Include tariffs, rescissions, privatization, donor-linked regulatory favors, federal stakes or direct bargaining with favored firms, and social-risk shifting when part of a coherent executive political economy.
Include public-goods cuts when paired with insider enrichment, contractor gain, or executive leverage.
Include crypto/AI or industrial-policy moves when tied to insider access and personalized discretion.
exclusion_notes: Exclude pure administrative-state capture unless economic governance or insider gain is central.
Exclude information manipulation about the economy unless it is integral to the economic-governance pattern.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_ADMINISTRATIVE_STATE_CAPTURE_AND_LOYALIST_PURGE, though both sometimes co-occur when economic agencies are politicized.
Adjacent to cand_INFO_CONTROL_AND_RECORD_MANIPULATION where economic statistics are manipulated to support this model.
Could later spawn sub-threads for tariffs/trade coercion versus insider tech/crypto favoritism.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with labels such as 'crony capitalism,' 'executive political economy,' 'tariff rule by decree,' or 'state-private fusion in economic governance'.
split_suggestions: Possible later split between 'tariff/emergency trade governance' and 'insider crony/state-capitalist deals'.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Tiered citizenship and targeted rollback of rights for disfavored groups
candidate_threads.description: Beyond immigration enforcement itself, multiple weeks show a recurring effort to redefine who counts as a full rights-bearing member of the polity. This includes attacks on birthright citizenship, reproductive autonomy, transgender inclusion, social-benefit access, veterans' care, education rights, and rights conditioned on ancestry, ideology, identity, or status. The throughline is a hierarchy of belonging and protection.

supporting_developments.development_title: Birthright citizenship, reproductive rights, and LGBTQ+ protections come under renewed attack
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly frames equal citizenship and bodily autonomy as being narrowed along status, gender, and sexuality lines.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration, gender, and benefits: stratifying citizenship and rights
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Strong evidence of rights hierarchy across immigration status, trans inclusion, and benefit access.

supporting_developments.development_title: Citizenship and Social Rights Are Reshaped Along Ancestry, Ideology, and Status Lines
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: One of the clearest formulations of the thread, combining ancestry rhetoric, welfare cuts, anti-trans policy, and voting hierarchy.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil and social rights are rolled back for veterans, migrants, LGBTQ+ people, and students
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows the hierarchy extending into veterans, students, migrants, and LGBTQ+ people across domains.

supporting_developments.development_title: Inequality is deepened through education, health, and disaster policy choices
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds policy mechanisms that burden vulnerable groups unequally and condition access on ideology or exclusion.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration enforcement and social policy deepen a tiered citizenship regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Explicitly names the thread and ties it to gender, education, reproductive care, and disability-related vulnerability.

inclusion_notes: Include attacks on birthright citizenship, reproductive autonomy, transgender rights, benefit access, and similar measures when they define different tiers of belonging or protection.
Include identity-based exclusions in health, education, veterans' benefits, or civic inclusion.
Include immigration-status differentiation when the emphasis is on normative hierarchy rather than enforcement machinery.
exclusion_notes: Exclude generic immigration raids or detention expansion unless the main point is rights hierarchy.
Exclude election engineering unless it directly concerns who counts as a member of the polity or eligible electorate.
boundary_notes: This thread overlaps substantially with cand_IMMIGRATION_AS_CARCERAL_AND_IDEOLOGICAL_CONTROL but is conceptually broader and more normative.
It also touches cand_RELIGION_AND_NATIONALIST_SYMBOLIC_ORDER when belonging is framed through bloodline, religion, or patriotic orthodoxy.
Within this window it is recurring but somewhat less continuously foregrounded than the immigration-enforcement thread.
merge_suggestions: Could merge later with labels like 'stratified citizenship,' 'hierarchy of belonging,' or 'rights rollback for marginalized groups'.
split_suggestions: Possible future split between 'citizenship/belonging' and 'bodily autonomy/gender/sexuality rights' if needed.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Attack on labor protections, unions, and organized counterpower
candidate_threads.description: In the second half of the window especially, labor protections and collective institutions are repeatedly targeted: cancellation of federal union contracts, removal of bargaining rights, wage and overtime rollbacks for care, disabled, contract, and federal workers, and policy structures that weaken organized labor as a counterweight. This is narrower than general inequality policy and distinct enough to preserve for later consolidation.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil service, unions, and independent data guardians are purged or politicized
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows cancellation of union contracts for hundreds of thousands of federal workers as part of state subordination.

supporting_developments.development_title: A sweeping assault on labor protections and unions reshapes the social contract
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly presents wage, overtime, bargaining, and contractor-protection rollback as a coordinated labor offensive.

supporting_developments.development_title: Labor, workers, and universities squeezed as economic policy favors elites
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Reinforces continuity through cancellation of bargaining for federal workers and anti-labor economic restructuring.

inclusion_notes: Include cancellation of union contracts, bargaining-rights removal, wage-floor cuts, overtime rollbacks, and allied anti-worker restructurings.
Useful as a preserved narrower thread because labor is repeatedly targeted as an institutional counterweight, not just as part of generic inequality.
exclusion_notes: Exclude broad anti-poverty or austerity measures unless they directly weaken labor institutions or protections.
Exclude general bureaucratic capture unless labor rights are central.
boundary_notes: Best treated as a sub-thread under broader administrative-state or political-economy patterns, but distinct enough to aid later consolidation.

Closely linked to cand_ADMINISTRATIVE_STATE_CAPTURE_AND_LOYALIST_PURGE when federal unions are targeted inside the state, and to cand_ECONOMIC_CRONYISM_AND_EXECUTIVE_POLITICAL_ECONOMY when labor losses accompany elite gain.
merge_suggestions: May later fold into a broader 'labor as counterpower targeted' thread if many windows show the same pattern.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Religion, nationalist memory, and symbolic politics used to legitimize power
candidate_threads.description: Several weeks show a recurring symbolic-cultural project: church-state boundary erosion, sacralized nationalism, Confederate or conquest imagery, rebranded military symbolism, state-curated monuments and honors, mandated classical/heritage aesthetics, and narrative elevation of regime-aligned heroes while dissident memories are erased. This is not merely culture-war rhetoric; it is state use of symbols and memory to define legitimate citizenship and authority.

supporting_developments.development_title: Religion and Nationalist Memory Recast as Tools of State Power
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly names the thread through workplace religiosity, nationalist imagery, ancestry rhetoric, and civic myth-making.

supporting_developments.development_title: Christian nationalism and exclusion reshape the Pentagon and civic equality
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows sectarian and Confederate symbolism embedded in the military and linked to exclusionary citizenship.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump escalates ideological control over information, history, and public memory
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds Smithsonian exhibit targeting and curated national memory to the symbolic-politics arc.

supporting_developments.development_title: Media, memory, and culture are reshaped to favor state-aligned narratives
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the thread through classical architecture mandates, Confederate imagery, and curated national identity.

supporting_developments.development_title: Religion and symbolism are harnessed to legitimize power and marginalize dissent
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Concentrates the thread in school prayer, religious speeches to troops, peace-vigil dismantling, partisan honors, and symbolic exclusion.

inclusion_notes: Include church-state erosion, military or civic symbolism, Confederate/conquest memory, state-curated monuments or honors, and official aesthetics/history battles.
Useful as a preserved distinct sub-thread because symbolic order repeatedly accompanies coercive governance and definitions of belonging.
exclusion_notes: Exclude general media disinformation unless symbolic memory or sacralized nationalism is central.
Exclude ordinary rights rollback unless framed through religion, national myth, or historical symbolism.
boundary_notes: This sub-thread overlaps with cand_INFO_CONTROL_AND_RECORD_MANIPULATION but is specifically about symbolic legitimacy, public ritual, and state-backed identity narratives.
It also overlaps with cand_TIERED_CITIZENSHIP_AND_TARGETED_RIGHTS where religion or bloodline is used to define belonging.
merge_suggestions: Could later merge with 'symbolic politics,' 'Christian nationalism,' or 'memory politics' candidates from other windows.

notes_on_window: The window shows unusually strong continuity around immigration enforcement as both a carceral apparatus and a broader theory of tiered belonging.
A later-window escalation is visible around domestic militarization and city-directed emergency governance, especially from weeks 30-34.
Information control is sustained across the entire window but changes form: from public media/data manipulation to archives, museums, AI propaganda, and scandal secrecy.
Election-engineering becomes more explicit and structural in the back half of the window, especially through redistricting, mail-voting attacks, and national voter-data ambitions.

Some week-specific developments on foreign policy alignment with Russia or on public health misinformation were important but less consistently present across the full 10-week window than the chosen core threads.
